$comment: Host notes of the independent review mechanism (docs/dev/independent-review-spec.md A7), read by observe in skills/hep-authoring/scripts/review.py. P1 covers Claude Code only. Paths use ~ for the home folder, <project> for the project root, <project-slug> for the project path with '/' replaced by '-', <uid> for the numeric user id, <tmp> for the system temporary folder /tmp (resolved, so /private/tmp on macOS) and <claude-config> for the Claude Code configuration folder ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.claude). The shared-directory patterns and the session start method are observed on the Claude Code CLI on macOS and confirmed by the maintainer (2026-10-21), but not documented by the host (documented: false). Without CLAUDE_PID (for example on a cloud host) the session start is unknown: isolation_not_yet_effective is then never raised and the report says the setting's effect cannot be confirmed (spec 7.3, last paragraph).

isolation.docs: Sub-agents docs, section 'Let Claude wait for a subagent': after setting it, run claude again from your shell, or open a new VS Code conversation
The docs say this rule prevents Claude from starting a fork, but not when it takes effect: a warning, with the R0 isolation self-check as the fallback

claude-code.dispatch_note: Name a non-fork subagent type when dispatching, whichever method is used.

session_start.note: the start time of the host process, which loaded the settings; absent variable: unknown (a warning)

conditional.note: v2.1.277 or later; read only when neither the working directory nor a parent has CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md does not count), unless the Project instructions setting says otherwise

instruction_files.imports: files pulled in by @path from any of the above
instruction_files.subagent_definition: the subagent definition file used for dispatch, with its memory and omitClaudeMd fields
